Process_Text.original: The billets for ECAP processing 4×4×40 mm³ in size were cut by spark erosion. They were then pressed at 423 K through an ECAP die with 4×4 mm² square channels intersecting at 90° with sharp corners.
Process_Text.simplified: ECAP at 423 K, 1 pass, die angle 90°, sharp corners, billet 4×4×40 mm³

Stage1.Note: Shared initial heat treatment per Section 3.

Structure_Text.original: The ECAP processed samples contained large populations of very thin deformation twins, and non-twinned regions with severely distorted grain microstructures and a high dislocation density. The microstructure appears to be non-homogeneous, comprising two major constituents with approximately equal volume fractions.
Structure_Text.simplified: UFG 316L after 1 ECAP pass: heterogeneous microstructure with ~50 vol% deformation twins and ~50 vol% dislocation-rich non-twinned regions

Volume_Fraction.Note: Twinned and non-twinned regions each approximately 50 vol%

Advanced_Quantitative_Features.microstructure_heterogeneity: two major constituents with approximately equal volume fractions: thin deformation twins and severely distorted dislocation-rich regions

Simulation_Metadata.Model_Type: Phenomenological dislocation-based constitutive model (Kocks-Mecking one-internal-variable approach)
Simulation_Metadata.Key_Equations: Eq. (8): σ(ε) = σ₀ + σₛ(1 - exp(-ε/ε̃)); Eq. (12): necking strain prediction; Eq. (13): Considère necking strain
Simulation_Metadata.Fitting_Method: Non-linear curve fitting of experimental true stress–true strain data using Eq. (8)
Constitutive_Assumptions: Single internal variable (total dislocation density ρ)

Key_Model_Parameters.sigma_0_definition: Back-extrapolated yield stress (includes Hall-Petch grain boundary strengthening)
